newsitem.title: UK: Britain clears CalEnergy's bid for Northern Electric.
newsitem.headline: Britain clears CalEnergy's bid for Northern Electric.

text.p: The British government has cleared Omaha-based CalEnergy Co. Inc.'s 782 million pound ($1.29 billion) hostile takeover bid for Northern Electric Plc, Trade and Industry Minister Ian Lang said Friday.
The clearance was announced just one week before the 650 pence-per-share ($10.76) offer by CalEnergy's CE Electric subsidiary was to close.

"CE Electric has given me assurances to address the regulatory concerns," Lang said in a statement. "These include assurances relating to Northern's financial and management resources and to maintaining Northern's financial status."

Lang said that with the assurances received he agreed with the British competition watchdog, the Office of Fair Trading, that there was no need to refer the case to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission for further consideration.
Just after the announcement, Northern Electric's share price leaped 42.5 pence (70 cents) to close at 645 pence ($10.67).
CE Electric, which launched its takeover offer with a 630 pence bid in October and later raised it to 650 pence, welcomed the ruling.

"I believe investors will now back the offer," CE Electric Chairman and Chief Executive David Sokol said in a statement. "They have seen it cleared and there is no white knight (bidder) on the horizon. We are now confident of getting above the 50 percent threshold.

"The decision for shareholders is now crystal clear," he added. "You just have to look at the facts. The stock was at 495 pence per share before we came in with our (first) bid (at 630 pence). The stock will plummet if it's not accepted. Add to that the fact that the (London Stock Exchange's) FTSE 100 index is looking at a correction. Here is an opportunity to take a very large profit, cash in the bank."
Northern has said it is worth more than 650 pence a share, with some analysts saying it is holding out for 700 pence.

In trying to fend off CE Energy the British electricity firm has outlined plans to realise value by merging its electricity and gas supply businesses with another regional player. It also wants to develop a 50 megawatt gas-fired power station in a joint venture with Rolls Royce.
Everything now hangs on how shareholders react, with both sides keeping up the campaign to clinch support from big investors.
CE Electric already owns 30 percent of Northern's shares and needs on 50 percent to prevail.
CalEnergy's stock added 12.5 cents to $28.25 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
